title: 🔥 The Roast: Week 10
preview: Maddox benched the flu game, the Commish started his newest quarterback, Cardillo started two inactives and won, Kyle benched a Patriot again, and Mike tried to buy Kirk Cousins. Tap if you can take it.
schedule_note: New roasts drop every Wednesday at 6 PM ET, right after waivers and before Thursday night.
intro: Week 9 gave us a five-touchdown quarterback on a bench, a -3.45 Monday night, two inactive starters in a winning lineup, and a three-way trade. And a public service announcement before we start: this league needs to learn what "so fucking back" means. One mediocre win doesn't get you there. Brad won one game after six straight losses. Not back. Cardillo won one and he's 6-12. Not back. Michigan State beat Michigan with five field goals and zero touchdowns. Not back. And the Commish? Guilty as charged, and sitting at 9-9. Week 10 kicks off Thursday. Nobody is safe.
facts_note: Every fact is real: Sleeper Week 9 results and lineups, transactions through Tuesday Nov 10, Week 10 matchups, NFL inactives and injury reports, and the ESPN archive for past seasons. Streaks are head-to-head only. A roast among friends.

entries.roast: BLASPHEMOUS! Michael Jordan had the flu in the 1997 Finals and dropped 38. C.J. Stroud had the flu Sunday and threw for 384 yards and FIVE touchdowns. 40.7 points! And where did Stroud play his flu game? On Jacob Maddox's BENCH! He started Malik Willis. MALIK! WILLIS! 3.6 points! The same Willis he defended in the chat. Buddy, you NEEDED a backup. Nobody said START him! You didn't have to die on the Willis hill! Start Stroud and you beat the Commish. But I guess he still has your number, Jacob, and you keep answering when he calls. The man owned the flu game and started the cough drop. Four straight wins, gone. Best record in the league, and he lost a game his own quarterback won. Stay off the court, Jacob. Whatever you've got, it's worse than the flu.
entries.this_week: vs Drew Hartman: 14-3-1 with a one-game skid, against 8-10 with a one-game skid. Maddox's first chance to prove he can lose to a team that isn't the Commish's.
entries.prediction: Maddox wins by 20 and leaves 30 on the bench out of habit.

entries.roast: The Commish beat Maddox, and he'd like a parade. Let's not throw one. Last week he bragged that he got "King Henry and a second off the waivers." Sunday, the King gave him 5.55. That's not a king. That's a guy in a Burger King crown handing you the wrong order. Wednesday he picks up Cam Ward, and almost immediately cuts him. For Drew Lock?! DREW LOCK?! And the win? Maddox started Malik Willis. Ryan didn't beat Maddox. Maddox lost, and Ryan was standing closest. Saturday, THE Dictator stood before his people and said, "I need to do better. I will be better. You all deserve better." Real dictators don't apologize. They don't promise to do better. And they definitely don't go 9-9. He writes the rules, approves every trade, runs the whole league, and still can't win his own rigged election.
entries.this_week: vs Mike Hemstreet: 9-9 riding a two-game streak, against 10-8 coming off a loss. Win, and THE Dictator is over .500 and insufferable about it.
entries.prediction: Ryan wins by 8 and calls it a mandate.

entries.roast: Listen, Brian. *Burp.* Your team's called Wubba Lubba Dub Ws. You know what "wubba lubba dub dub" actually means? "I am in great pain, please help me." Last year that wasn't a team name, Brian. That was a cry for help. Reigning champ, goes 3-11, dead last, and Cardillo walks off with the Belt. Now he's 13-5 and walking around like the smartest man in the multiverse. Champion, to 3-11, to 13-5. The Dark Knight trilogy took nine years and three movies. Brian did it with a lineup he barely touches. That's not a genius, Brian. That's a Jerry who wandered into the one dimension where the other nine guys forgot how to set a lineup. Wubba lubba dub dub.
entries.this_week: vs Nick Cardillo: 13-5 and coming off a win, against 6-12 and coming off a win. The hero gets the softest Sunday of his comeback, which is exactly how he likes them.
entries.prediction: Brian wins by 30, and somebody in the chat calls it luck again.

entries.roast: Bradley. Son. Come here. The whole league is so proud of you. Saturday you sent us a video and said, "I'm not having a good time right now." You told us Drew would put up 200 on you. Drew didn't come close, and after six straight losses you went out there and won a football game. We know it wasn't easy. You own Josh Allen and Patrick Mahomes, the two best quarterbacks on Earth, and CeeDee Lamb outscored both of them combined. Your wide receiver carried your entire quarterback room, buddy, and we're still proud. You started Kamara with a better back on the bench, and that's okay. You started Egbuka with a better receiver on the bench, and that's okay too. Every kid gets a trophy, Bradley. Now go wait in the car. Your mother and I need to talk about the other ten losses.
entries.this_week: vs Taylor Alvarado: 7-10-1 with one win in a row, against 4-14 and four straight losses. For the first time all year, Brad is the bully.
entries.prediction: Brad wins by 15 and asks if it counts double.

entries.roast: Kyle. Kyle. You're Gronk Nation. Gronk Nation FOR LIFE, it's right there in your username. Two weeks ago you benched the Patriots, and we let it go. We figured okay, one time, the guy's going through something. Sunday you do it AGAIN. Rhamondre Stevenson, a New England Patriot, sitting on your bench. And who'd you start? D'Andre Swift. A Chicago Bear! You move to Chicago and all of a sudden you're starting Bears over Patriots? Stevenson outscored Swift by more than you lost by. Three-game streak, dead, to a 6-12 team. And the one Patriot you DID stay loyal to? The Patriots defense, on your bench, scoring negative points. So Tuesday you cut them. He benches the Patriots who score and rosters the ones who don't. That's not a fan, Kyle. That's a guy who wears the jersey to the bar and roots for whoever's buying.
entries.this_week: vs Nicholas Kasik: 9-9 off a loss, against 9-9 off a win. Winner gets a winning record. Loser gets Taylor's sympathy card.
entries.prediction: Kyle wins by 6 and starts a Bear anyway.

entries.roast: Kasik scored 186.6, the highest score of the week, and he'd like a moment. Here's the moment. He did it against Taylor, the worst team in the league. That's not a resume. That's beating your little brother at Madden and getting it framed. And even against Taylor he couldn't set a clean lineup: Zay Flowers started for 5.3 with Caleb Douglas' 13.0 on the bench. Bed, Bath, and Bijan. Named after a chain that went bankrupt, which is the most honest thing about this roster. Nine and nine. The 20 percent off coupon of fantasy football: everybody has one in a drawer, and nobody remembers it until it's expired.
entries.this_week: vs Kyle Llano: 9-9 off a win, against 9-9 off a loss. Same record, opposite streaks, and the winner gets to call himself a contender until Tuesday.
entries.prediction: Kasik loses by 6 and calls 186 against Taylor a trend.

entries.roast: *Ring.* Shame. Sunday morning, about 90 minutes before kickoff, the Cowboys declared George Pickens inactive. Cardillo started him. *Ring.* Shame. Sunday morning, Ian Rapoport reported Kyle Monangai wouldn't play. Cardillo started him. *Ring.* Shame. Two inactives, announced in broad daylight, with healthy players sitting right there on the bench, and the defending champion started both of them anyway. Two zeros. And he won, which is worse, because now he thinks it worked. Then there's the Herbert trade. Cardillo got Baker and a pile of picks, and Baker spent Sunday on Cardillo's bench matching what Herbert did for Mike. He won the trade and benched the prize. Strip him. Shave him. Walk him through King's Landing. The defending champ won a football game with two empty chairs in his lineup, and he'd like you to call that a title defense. Shame. Shame. SHAME.
entries.this_week: vs Brian Mulvihill: 6-12 off a win, against 13-5 off a win. The defending champ is 6-12, and the only thing he's defending Sunday is his spot above Taylor.
entries.prediction: Brian wins by 30, and Cardillo still introduces himself as the defending champ.

entries.roast: Jordan Belfort's Nuts. Perfect name, because Drew is the Wolf of Sleeper Street. Eight trades this season, the most in the league. Drew makes trades like Belfort made money. Fast, loud, and the feds are going to look at all of it. Sell me this pen? Drew already traded the pen, traded for it again, and asked for a second. Wednesday, the three-way: Derrick Henry goes out, Jameson Williams comes in. Sunday, Williams' first start for Drew: 5.0. Then he benches Denzel Boston and Isaiah Likely, 16.3 apiece, for Jalen Coker and Sam LaPorta, 13.8 combined. Loses to Brad. BRAD! A man on a six-game losing streak. And then the NFL traded Drew's own quarterback to Minnesota without even calling him. First deal of the season Drew wasn't in on. He's not the Wolf of Wall Street. He's the guy at the Stratton Oakmont fax machine wondering why nobody cc'd him.
entries.this_week: vs Jacob Maddox: 8-10 off a loss, against 14-3-1 off a loss. Drew has until Sunday to trade for Maddox's lineup.
entries.prediction: Maddox wins by 20, and Drew calls it a buying opportunity.

entries.roast: Dearly beloved, we are gathered here today to lay to rest the 2026 season of Taylor Alvarado. RIP. He is survived by the lowest score in the league three weeks running, the fewest points of anyone in the league, and a record of 4-14. Sunday, Kasik beat him by 78.75, the worst beating of the week, and we ask that you not speak ill of the departed, because frankly there's nothing left to say. His receiver Ladd McConkey made it to pregame warmups, took one look around, and spent the afternoon not playing. Zero. Even his players won't stay for the whole service. In lieu of flowers, the family asks that you stop scheduling Taylor. He has suffered enough, and so has his bench. Ashes to ashes, waivers to waivers. Please bow your heads. He's lost four straight, and nobody is coming to the reception.
entries.this_week: vs Bradley Kochheiser: 4-14 and four straight losses, against 7-10-1 off a win. The good news at the funeral: for the first time since 2023, Kirk Cousins is throwing to Taylor's Justin Jefferson. Rejoice.
entries.prediction: Brad wins by 15, and Jefferson sends Taylor flowers.

entries.roast: I tell ya, Mike gets no respect. None! Mike, this is a DYNASTY league. On October 14 he trades Ollie Gordon for TreVeyon Henderson, a young home-run hitter, a top-20 dynasty running back. RB20! Three weeks later he tells the chat, "Traveyon Henderson is for sale." The next morning he cuts him for nothing. Well, for Carson Wentz. Same thing. He listed a Ferrari and took a shopping cart. He held Henderson for 22 days. In a dynasty league! People keep gym memberships in January longer than that. This guy plans for the future like he's buying milk by the day. Monday night, Wentz goes 8-for-25, two picks, a lost fumble, and gets benched for Max Brosmer. -3.45! Daniel Jones scored 11.6 on Mike's bench. Start Jones and Mike beats Brian. Then the Vikings trade for Kirk Cousins to replace Wentz, and Mike offers Drew Jalen Hurts and a third. For Kirk Cousins! Mike's quarterbacks this week: Wentz, Herbert, Jones, and a trade offer. That's not a depth chart. That's a line at a pawn shop. The Vikings were desperate for a quarterback. Mike is desperate for the Vikings' quarterback. A quarterback the Vikings already let walk once! I tell ya, desperation has a type.
entries.this_week: vs Ryan Nussdorfer: 10-8 off a loss, against 9-9 on a two-game streak. Mike's still shopping for a quarterback, and his opponent is the one man in the league who has to approve the receipt.
entries.prediction: Ryan wins by 8, and Mike starts whichever quarterback answered his texts.
